cohort: The cohort consisted of 233 non-anomalous, singleton pregnancies with fetal growth restriction who received umbilical artery Doppler assessment at the study institution from 2009 to 2020.
finding: Intermittent absent end-diastolic flow in growth-restricted pregnancies is associated with a similar rate of composite neonatal morbidity as persistently elevated Doppler waveforms, with no significant difference between Doppler groups after adjusting for gestational age at delivery and antenatal steroids.
